notes: Both with_skill evals hit 10/10 and both used the correct labs-page.json filename convention, the FAQ-accordion pattern for troubleshooting, and folded task hints into their accordion tabs verbatim - fully consistent across both real labs.

The without_skill baseline scored surprisingly high (90%) because CLAUDE.md already spells out the reference-tier rule, the live-palette override, and the publish go-ahead requirement in detail - a thorough project CLAUDE.md closes most of the gap a skill would normally open. The skill still adds value, but this project is not a case of "baseline fails badly without a skill."

The one genuine content-completeness gap: the without_skill run for dedupe-late-arriving-orders silently dropped both Task 3 and Task 4 hints from page-content.md, while the without_skill run for investigate-duplicate-orders correctly kept its hints. The with_skill run got hints right in both evals (2/2 vs baseline's 1/2) - this inconsistency, not an outright inability, is the clearest evidence the skill's explicit widget-mapping reference adds real value.

Both without_skill runs used elementor/landing-page.json (the existing course-output convention) instead of the skill's labs-page.json convention - expected, since baseline had no way to know that name. This is a naming-consistency win for the skill (useful for any future automation keyed on that path) rather than a content-quality issue, and the "labs-page.json" filename assertion in evals 0/1 should be read that way rather than as a baseline failure.

The nonexistent-slug-refusal eval does not discriminate between with/without skill - both correctly refused to fabricate content and pointed at a lab-creation step, purely from CLAUDE.md's own rules. Worth keeping as a regression guard, but it will not show skill value going forward.
No run of either configuration attempted a live Novamira/Angie call or simulated a "yes" - the dry-run safety constraint held across all 6 runs.
This was a single run per configuration (not the usual 3), so pass-rate deltas here are indicative, not statistically robust - worth another pass at 3 runs/config if the skill changes materially.
